correctness.rationale: For e_i e_j=e_{2j-i} (indices mod p), the coefficient derivation identity is c_{2j-i}(u)=c_i(2j-u)+c_j((u+i)/2). Writing F_i(r)=c_i(i+r) and re-centering gives F_{i+2d}(r)=F_i(-r)+F_{i+d}(r/2). Taking d=0, eliminating F_i(-r), and using 2 invertible shows i->F_i(r)-F_0(r) has translation-independent differences, hence is additive F_p->K and equals alpha(r)i. F_i(r)=alpha(r)i+beta(r), both vanish at 0. The remaining conditions alpha(-r)=-alpha(r), alpha(r/2)=2alpha(r), beta(r)=beta(-r)+beta(r/2) diagonalize in the Vandermonde basis r^t on F_p^×. Both permit exactly odd exponents t with 2^{t+1}=1, and each yields independent alpha- and beta-derivations. The count of allowable t is (p-1)/lcm(ord_p(2),2), giving the dimension 2 times this count for any field K of characteristic p. An independent linear-system derivation-nullity test over F_3,F_5,F_7 returned 2,2,2 and verified basis-space completeness for those sizes only.
